title: Generic common-stage pair-category and coherent family data
statement: Fix a directed poset $I$ in the universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. A normalized additive transition diagram consists of categories $C_i$, additive transition functors $U_{i\leq j}$, identity comparisons, associative transition comparisons, and their unit and pentagon equations. Its common-stage pair data consists of pair objects $(i,X)$; representatives over a common stage with source and target inequalities and an arrow between the transported objects; transport by the specified associator inverse on the source and associator on the target; eventual equality after a further common stage; and the quotient Hom type and representative class. A pair structure supplies the additive-group, identity, composition, and additive composition laws on this quotient, with its object carrier, representative map, category and preadditive instances, and an `IsCanonical` predicate requiring the representative formulas for equality, identities, composition, addition, zero, and negation. For two such diagrams, a family consists of additive stage functors and comparison isomorphisms between each transition after applying the source and target functor; `Family.Coherent` requires the normalized unit and tower equations. The family has its literal object and representative formulas. Finally, `IsDescent` for pair structures, a family, and a functor records the literal object formula, the representative map formula, and additivity. These are the generic common-stage notions used by the pair-functor descent theorem; no existence or uniqueness assertion is included.
